jim-a.desc: An Essex market trader of about fifty-five: cheerful, chancing, quick patter, a warm rough voice that has shouted prices across a field for thirty years.

jim-b.desc: A Black Country man of about fifty-five, a car-boot regular: friendly, matter-of-fact, flat West Midlands vowels, as if selling a kettle.

jim-c.desc: A South London wheeler-dealer of about fifty-five: cocky, sing-song, a wink in every word, a bit of a geezer.

phineas-a.desc: A very old-money English man of about sixty-five from the shires: plummy, slow, bored, deep and fruity, used to never being refused.

phineas-b.desc: A self-made Yorkshire millionaire of about sixty-five: gruff, blunt, low, quietly menacing, every word a decision.

phineas-c.desc: A Home Counties financier of about sixty-five: smooth, soft, oily, faintly amused, speaks as if dictating to a secretary.

badcode-a.desc: A Cornish man of about fifty, a village auctioneer: kind, unhurried, gentle but firm, like a vicar running the tombola.

badcode-b.desc: A Liverpool man of about forty, an auctioneer: dry, quick, deadpan, polite with an edge.

badcode-c.desc: A Northumberland man of about sixty, an auctioneer: calm, clear, plain-spoken, warm, utterly unimpressed by money.
